source_text:
Ὃν ἐπίσκοπον ἔγνων οὐκ ἀφ̓ ἑαυτοῦ οὐδὲ δἰ ἀνθρώπων κεκτῆσθαι τὴν διακονίαν τὴν εἰς τὸ κοινὸν ἀνήκουσαν οὐδὲ κατὰ κενοδοξίαν, ἀλλ’ ἐν ἀγάπῃ θεοῦ πατρὸς καὶ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ: οὗ καταπέπληγμαι τὴν ἐπιείκειαν, ὃς σιγῶν πλείονα δύναται τῶν μάταια λαλούντων.
συνευρύθμισται γαρ ταῖς ἐντολαῖς ὡς χορδαῖς κιθάρα. διὸ μακαρίζει μου ἡ ψυχὴ τὴν εἰς θεὸν αὐτοῦ γνώμην, ἐπιγνοὺς ἐνάρετον καὶ τέλειον οὖσαν, τὸ ἀκίνητον αὐτοῦ καὶ τὸ ἀόργητον αὐτοῦ ἐν πάσῃ ἐπιεικείᾳ θεοῦ ζῶντος.
thought_title: The bishop's ministry is from God, not from himself
orientation: Ignatius is praising the bishop of Philadelphia, whom he has met, and explaining why the bishop's quiet gentleness is powerful.
pass_a_gloss: Whom [as] bishop I knew not from himself nor through men to have acquired the ministry the [one] for the common [good] belonging, nor according to vainglory, but in love of God [the] Father and of [the] Lord Jesus Christ; at whose gentleness I am astonished, who being silent more is able than those speaking vain things. For he has been fitted together with the commandments as [with] strings [of] a lyre. Therefore blesses my soul his toward God disposition, having recognized [it] virtuous and perfect being, the immovableness of him and the without-anger of him in all gentleness of [the] living God.

choices.term: τὴν διακονίαν τὴν εἰς τὸ κοινὸν ἀνήκουσαν
choices.english: the ministry that belongs to the common good
choices.why: The participle ἀνήκουσαν means 'belonging to' or 'pertaining to,' and τὸ κοινόν here means the shared community; rendering it as 'the common good' keeps the communal scope of the bishop's service.
κενοδοξία is a compound of 'empty' and 'glory'; 'vainglory' preserves the negative moral sense of self-display rather than a neutral 'empty reputation.'
The verb is a compound of συν- ('together') and εὐρυθμίζω ('to set in rhythm'); 'fitted together' captures the harmonious alignment with the commandments that the lyre image develops.

choices.term: τὸ ἀκίνητον αὐτοῦ καὶ τὸ ἀόργητον αὐτοῦ
choices.english: his immovableness and his freedom from anger
choices.why: The neuter substantives with the article name qualities; 'immovableness' and 'freedom from anger' render them as stable character traits rather than momentary states.
rejected: his being unmoved and his being without anger

choices.english: in all the gentleness of the living God
choices.why: The phrase qualifies the bishop's qualities as participating in God's own gentleness; 'living God' is a fixed biblical epithet and should not be weakened.
rejected: in all gentleness before the living God
with all the gentleness of a living God

pass_b_english: I have come to know this bishop, and I am certain that he did not receive his ministry for the common good from himself or through human beings, nor out of vainglory, but in the love of God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. I am astonished at his gentleness: though he is silent, he has more power than those who speak empty words.

For he is attuned to the commandments like strings on a lyre. That is why my soul blesses his disposition toward God, for I have recognized that it is virtuous and perfect: his steadfastness and his freedom from anger, all in the gentleness of the living God.

polish.changed: Clarified that Ignatius is the speaker throughout, made the pronoun references explicit (the bishop, his gentleness, his disposition), and smoothed the sentence rhythm while preserving every claim and qualification exactly.

notes.why: Reader may not realize 'council of elders' = 'elders' = presbyterion, and 'council of the apostles' is a typological parallel, not a different group.
notes.fix: Use consistent 'council of elders' with note; clarify 'council of the apostles' as typology.

notes.why: 'Passible' (capable of suffering) vs 'passion' (suffering/death) are related but distinct; reader may miss Christological point.
notes.fix: Gloss 'passible' as 'capable of suffering' on first use.

notes.why: Reader may think 'council of the apostles' is a historical body separate from 'council of elders', not realizing it's a typological parallel.
notes.fix: Add note: 'council of the apostles' typologically parallels 'council of elders'.

notes.quote: council of elders of the church

variants.text: council of elders of the church

notes.why: Same entity as 'council of elders' elsewhere; 'of the church' adds no distinction but may confuse.

polish.changed: Clarified that the bishop, not the commandments, is fitted like strings on a lyre, and smoothed the sentence rhythm for reading aloud.

notes.why: Same Greek presbyterion rendered with and without parenthetical 'presbyters', risking confusion.
notes.fix: Use consistent 'council of elders' with note.

notes.quote: council of elders in the place of the council of the apostles
notes.why: Same word 'council' used for presbyterion and apostolic group, but different Greek words may be involved; still risks conflation.
notes.fix: Note Greek terms or use 'college of apostles' if distinct.

notes.quote: He is fitted together with the commandments like strings on a lyre
notes.why: Bishop fitted with commandments? Usually people are strings; commandments are not.
notes.fix: Check Greek; may mean 'he is tuned to the commandments' or 'harmonized with'.

polish.changed: Clarified that the bishop's silence is a deliberate restraint rather than literal muteness, and smoothed the sentence flow for reading aloud while preserving every claim and qualification.

notes.quote: by keeping silent he has more power than those who speak empty words
notes.why: 'Keeping silent' seems to mean 'restraint' or 'gentleness', not literal silence; reader may misunderstand.
notes.fix: Revise to 'by his restraint' or add note.

problems.why: Same Greek word (presbyterion) rendered differently; 'council of the apostles' and 'council of God' may confuse readers about whether these are the same body.
problems.fix: Use 'council of elders' consistently; note 'council of the apostles' as metaphor.

problems.quote: his immovableness and his freedom from anger, all in the gentleness of the living God
problems.why: 'Immovableness' (Greek: a-kinesia?) is awkward; likely 'steadfastness' or 'unwavering constancy'.

edits.old: his immovableness and his freedom from anger
edits.new: his steadfastness and his freedom from anger

fixed: The glossary issue about 'council of elders' does not appear in this section; no change needed here.
Changed 'immovableness' to 'steadfastness' to avoid awkwardness while preserving the sense of the Greek.

problems.why: Same institution alternates between 'council of elders' and plain 'elders'; reader may think these differ.
problems.fix: Use consistent term or gloss as 'body of elders/presbyters'.

problems.quote: he is fitted together with the commandments like strings on a lyre
problems.why: 'Fitted together with the commandments' is odd; likely 'attuned to the commandments'.
problems.fix: 'attuned to the commandments like strings on a lyre'.

edits.old: he is fitted together with the commandments like strings on a lyre
edits.new: he is attuned to the commandments like strings on a lyre

fixed: The glossary problem is not a mistranslation: the source uses πρεσβυτέριον only where 'council of elders' appears, and the plain 'elders' in this section is not from that term, so no change is needed.
The mistranslation is real: συνευρύθμισται means 'has been fitted/attuned together with', and 'attuned to the commandments' better conveys the musical metaphor of strings on a lyre.
